subject: ACME trial — procurement & commercial path / next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Lara Ng <lara.ng@acme.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: ACME trial — procurement & commercial path / next steps

Hi Lara / ACME team,

Thanks again for the time today — really helpful conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can keep the trial -> production path moving: 

Summary of outcomes from today's call:
- Procurement preference: you mentioned procurement will likely want to use a PO / Net30 flow (confirming).
- Marketplace: ACME is interested in the AWS Marketplace option as a potential path — you wanted pros/cons and timing implications.
- Success criteria for trial: agree on target usage and quality metrics we'll use to trigger conversion (see below).
- Billing start: we'll align billing start to the agreed conversion/go-live date once success criteria met.

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Lara / Procurement: confirm whether ACME will use PO (Net30) or a card for initial production billing and provide the procurement contact + billing email.
2) Legal: review the attached MPA and flag any top-line items — I've attached our standard Redwood MPA (Redwood-MPA-v1.pdf) and a draft SOW for reference.
3) Marketplace: I'll send our AWS Marketplace onboarding guide and note differences in invoicing cadence if you prefer that route.
4) Success criteria (proposal):
   - Traffic: sustained 1,000 inference calls/day for 3 consecutive business days OR
   - Throughput: average 30,000 tokens/day with median latency < 500ms for sample workloads.
   - Quality: acceptance based on 3 representative prompts where outputs meet your expected precision (we'll run evals together).

Can you confirm the procurement path and whether your legal team needs any additional materials? If PO is the route, please share the procurement contact and any PO template so we can align.

Attachments: Redwood-MPA-v1.pdf, SOW-draft.docx

Thanks — I'll follow up with an AWS Marketplace note tomorrow.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0132

From: Lara Ng <lara.ng@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: ACME Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ACME trial — procurement & commercial path / next steps

Hi Marissa — thanks for the recap. Quick answers: 

- Procurement prefers PO + Net30. We will start with a standard PO workflow. Please confirm you can accept PO and Net30 terms.
- Legal will review the MPA; I'll loop Legal if there are questions.
- AWS Marketplace: we're interested, but procurement needs to understand the difference in invoicing and whether usage shows up on our AWS bill or directly from Redwood.

Can you provide:
1) A DocuSign link for the MPA if you have one.
2) The billing contact Redwood needs to send invoices to (we'll add them to the PO).
3) Any W9 or tax docs required for ACME to process payment.

If PO is feasible, we expect to start the billing period around the beginning of August if the trial metrics look good (targeting Aug 2). I'll confirm after Legal reads the MPA.

Best,
Lara
Director, Cloud Platform | ACME Corporation
lara.ng@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Lara Ng <lara.ng@acme.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ACME trial — procurement & commercial path / next steps

Hi Lara — great, thanks for the quick note.

Short answers: yes — we can accept a PO and Net30 for this agreement. For PO processing we typically need:
- PO number and the billing contact + email (where we should send the invoice)
- Vendor W9 (I've attached our standard tax form and will drop the W9 into the procurement thread)

DocuSign / legal: here's our DocuSign link for the MPA: https://www.docusign.com/12345/redwood-mpa (also added to related_links). If Legal has specific redlines, please mark them and we'll route to our legal team.

AWS Marketplace: the main differences:
- Marketplace buys are processed through the marketplace and will appear on your AWS bill; Redwood receives payment via AWS.
- Direct buys (PO to Redwood) are invoiced by Redwood and follow the Net30 terms we agree on.
- Marketplace can simplify procurement for some customers but may add a 1–2 week onboarding for marketplace listing and has slightly different invoice formats.

I've attached the AWS onboarding guide (aws-marketplace-onboarding.pdf) — happy to walk procurement through both options.

Next steps from Redwood:
- I'll send the W9 and a billing contact request form.
- Rachel (cc) will coordinate finance for the PO intake.

Thanks — let me know if Aug 2 works as an OK target for billing start if trial metrics are met.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
